fields.title: Nothing checks a page or the output for accessibility

sections.What it checks:
* [std-A11Y.STRUCT](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/b0333383184268b860732fbaaad3e8631faa0ba1/examples/dog-fooding/standards/accessibility.md#struct-a-markdown-author-owns-the-structure-of-a-page) says heading levels "**MUST** descend one at a time".
* It says an image "**MUST** have alternative text saying what a reader who cannot see it needs".
* [std-A11Y.COLOUR](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/b0333383184268b860732fbaaad3e8631faa0ba1/examples/dog-fooding/standards/accessibility.md#colour-kac-carries-no-meaning-in-colour-alone) says output "**MUST** stay complete when colour is off".
sections.How it works:
Nothing runs. The checks these rules need are two jobs on each pull request:

* markdownlint over `docs/`, with `MD001` (`heading-increment`) and `MD045` (`no-alt-text`) turned on, failing the
  `docs` job on a finding.
* A test that runs each verb twice, with `NO_COLOR=1` and with colour on. It strips the escape sequences from the
  second run and fails where the runs print different words.
sections.Coverage and gaps:
A reviewer reading the diff is the only thing that notices any of these today.

The checks would prove a heading order, an alternative text, and words that survive without colour. They would not prove that link text makes sense out of context. Nobody has read either surface with a screen reader. The theme's contrast, focus and keyboard rules go unchecked. So does every rule under [std-A11Y.GAPS](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/b0333383184268b860732fbaaad3e8631faa0ba1/examples/dog-fooding/standards/accessibility.md#gaps-what-falls-short-is-written-down-where-a-reader-finds-it) and [std-A11Y.WORSE](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/b0333383184268b860732fbaaad3e8631faa0ba1/examples/dog-fooding/standards/accessibility.md#worse-a-change-that-makes-either-surface-worse-needs-a-deviation).

[ctl-assessed-pin-tests](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/b0333383184268b860732fbaaad3e8631faa0ba1/examples/dog-fooding/controls/assessed-pin-tests.md) checks two rules under [std-A11Y.ASSESS](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/b0333383184268b860732fbaaad3e8631faa0ba1/examples/dog-fooding/standards/accessibility.md#assess-a-pinned-component-carries-an-accessibility-assessment): that an assessment names the pinned version, and that a pin moving its major or minor brings a new one. Below 0.1.0 any move of the pin brings a new one. [#967](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/issues/967) found the second unchecked after Dependabot moved `Spectre.Console.Cli` in [#802](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/pull/802). The other rules under it go unchecked.
